writeup: TIC 229205551 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 5.835269 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 26.69%, while no secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates from the target location, with a centroid offset of 1.5 arcsec and a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 54.6. The detection achieved a very high significance in the automated search algorithm (signal-to-noise of 1890.6), and the system does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the initially measured period was actually half the true orbital period. This depth variation pattern is an open question requiring further investigation to fully characterize this candidate system.
